title: Transporting a Panhard Dyna Z12 after purchase: what to anticipate
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: Bringing a Dyna Z12 home does not always mean simply driving away. When the car has stood still for a long time, the right transport protects both the vehicle and the restoration project that is about to begin.
content:
Bringing a Dyna Z12 home does not always mean turning the key and taking the motorway. When the car has stood still for a long time, when the brakes are uncertain or when the distance is heavy, transport on a trailer becomes a normal part of the project.

Do not confuse a running engine with a road-ready car

An old car can start correctly and still be unfit for a long journey home. Brakes, tyres, fuel system, air cooling, electrics and directional stability have to be judged together. On an unknown car, that check matters more than a brief idle test.

When in doubt, the trailer often costs less than a forced drive home or a breakdown far from the garage.

Prepare the loading properly

Width, ground clearance, access, strapping points, wheel condition and low-speed manoeuvrability should all be thought through before the transporter arrives. A light Dyna is still vulnerable around its weak areas, so loading has to be clean and unhurried.

Careful loading already belongs to the restoration. It protects structure as much as mechanics.

Documents, parts and the departure context

The departure is also the right moment to collect papers, removed parts, small fittings and everything that tells the recent history of the car. A forgotten box in the seller's garage can save weeks of searching later.

The more orderly the departure, the more useful the arrival becomes.

Arrival marks the real first step

Once the car is home, it is important to resist the urge to drive immediately. The better reflex is to check fluids, brakes, battery and leaks calmly, then decide on a serious recommissioning plan. When transport is done well, it clears the way for the real work.

This reference belongs with the page Our Panhard Dyna Z12 in the Gulf of Saint-Tropez. In the same theme, you can also read how to recommission a stored Dyna Z12.
